# TeX Live packages installed by .github/workflows/latex-build-deploy.yml.
#
# This is the DEFAULT manifest, shared by every repository that calls the
# reusable workflow. A repository that needs something not listed here can drop
# its own .github/texlive-packages.txt in beside its workflow; the build prefers
# the caller's copy and falls back to this one. Prefer adding the package here,
# though -- a local manifest is a copy that has to be maintained, which is the
# thing this arrangement exists to avoid.
#
# This file is the cache key for the CI TeX Live installation: change it and the
# next run reinstalls from scratch, leave it alone and every run restores the
# same tree in seconds. That is the whole point of keeping it explicit rather
# than installing `texlive-full`.
#
# The list below was derived mechanically from main.fls: every file pdflatex and
# biber actually opened, mapped back to the TeX Live package that ships it,
# taking the union over the template and the notes repositories that share it.
# tlmgr pulls dependencies in automatically, so only direct requirements belong
# here. Beyond the base scheme, collections (collection-latexrecommended and
# friends) are deliberately not used: they drag in some 800 packages for the
# sake of a handful.
#
# A \usepackage names a style file, which is not always the name of the TeX
# Live package shipping it -- authblk lives in preprint, tikz in pgf. Where the
# two differ, the entry carries a `# provides:` annotation naming the style
# files it is here for. .github/scripts/check-manifest.sh reads those and fails
# the build, before anything is installed, if the sources load something this
# file does not account for.
#
# So: adding a \usepackage means either adding its TeX Live package here
# (`tlmgr info foo.sty` names it), or -- if some entry already installs it --
# adding the style file to that entry's `provides:` list.
#
# Blank lines and #-comments are ignored.

# --- Base ------------------------------------------------------------------
# install-tl bootstraps scheme-infraonly (tlmgr and nothing else), so the base
# distribution is requested here like everything else -- that keeps the cache
# key honest, since bumping the base invalidates it too.
scheme-basic

# --- Build tooling ----------------------------------------------------------
latexmk
biber
biblatex
logreq

# --- Document class and core LaTeX -----------------------------------------
latex     # provides: book, fontenc, inputenc
tools     # provides: array, bm, longtable, verbatim
appendix
l3kernel
l3packages
l3backend
etoolbox
xkeyval
iftex

# --- Fonts ------------------------------------------------------------------
amsfonts  # provides: amssymb
cm-super
sansmathfonts
jknapltx  # provides: mathrsfs
rsfs
psnfss    # provides: pifont

# --- Page layout and typography --------------------------------------------
geometry
fancyhdr
lastpage
parskip
setspace
ragged2e
preprint  # provides: authblk
enumitem
csquotes
babel
babel-english

# --- Maths ------------------------------------------------------------------
amsmath
amscls    # provides: amsthm
mathtools
mathdots
cancel
xfrac
yhmath

# --- Tables, floats, figures -----------------------------------------------
booktabs
float
wrapfig
caption   # provides: subcaption
graphics  # provides: graphicx
graphics-cfg
graphics-def

# --- Graphics and diagrams --------------------------------------------------
pgf       # provides: tikz
pgfplots
pict2e
tikz-cd
tikz-3dplot
qtree
xcolor

# --- Boxes, listings, notes -------------------------------------------------
tcolorbox
tikzfill
environ
trimspaces
listings
listingsutf8
todonotes
pdfcol

# --- References and links ---------------------------------------------------
hyperref
cleveref
url
hycolor
bookmark

# --- Filler text used by the template --------------------------------------
blindtext
lipsum

# --- PDF inclusion ----------------------------------------------------------
pdfpages
pdflscape
eso-pic
